Review this exact FG-177 cleanup-new-halt ownership repair. Requirements: inherited FinallyUnwind permission admits cleanup calls after the original hosted halt; a newer engine-level call refusal inside cleanup must stop all same-block successors, remain opaque to Groovy catch, and still execute nested finally; a catchable shell StepFailed may recover inside cleanup; nested finally return must replace both pending halts as measured on Jenkins 2.568.1; an escaping refusal must transfer its precise reason to retry/top-level ownership with unchanged durable semantics. Audit Stop exception precedence, wrapper catchHostedHalt ownership, retries, nested wrappers, helper/argument suppression, accidental catchability, diagnostics, and receipt/test false positives. Four new tier-1 cases must genuinely cover the claims and the previous seven FG-177 cases must remain unchanged. Return VERDICT and ACTION ITEMS.\n\nEXACT STAGED DIFF:\ndiff --git a/differential/cases/fg177-cleanup-catch-recovery.Jenkinsfile b/differential/cases/fg177-cleanup-catch-recovery.Jenkinsfile

--- /dev/null
+++ b/differential/cases/fg177-cleanup-catch-recovery.Jenkinsfile
@@ -0,0 +1,23 @@
+pipeline {
+  agent any
+  stages {
+    stage('cleanup-catch-recovery') {
+      steps {
+        script {
+          try {
+            sh('original', 'extra')
+          } finally {
+            try {
+              sh 'exit 7'
+            } catch (Exception caught) {
+              echo "cleanup-caught:${caught}"
+            }
+            echo 'cleanup-recovered'
+          }
+          echo 'after-must-not-run'
+        }
+      }
+    }
+  }
+  post { failure { echo 'terminal-failure' } }
+}
